 ‘Django Unchained’ Showed Leonardo DiCaprio’s Villainous Side
 MOVIE NEWS 
 November 14, 2026 
 By Ari Coine 
 Image Source: Amazon 
 Leonardo DiCaprio’s body of work includes many difficult characters. But Calvin Candie is someone you wouldn’t want to cross paths with, let alone lock eyes with. The mercurial plantation owner in Django Unchained gave DiCaprio a chance to play a far more sinister character. It also marked his first film with director Quentin Tarantino . They later reunited for Once Upon a Time in Hollywood .
 Looking back, it was quite an introduction to their working relationship. There was no warm-up act for DiCaprio in Django Unchained . He stepped straight into the shoes of a character we were meant to loathe.
 ‘ Django Unchained’ follows a man’s quest to free his wife 
 Jamie Foxx leads Django Unchained (2012) as Django, an enslaved man whose encounter with a bounty hunter leads to freedom. That bounty hunter is Dr. King Schultz ( Christoph Waltz ), who becomes his unlikely partner. Django learns to track fugitives, but his true goal is personal. He wants to find and free his beloved wife, Broomhilda ( Kerry Washington ).
 Their search leads to Candyland, the sprawling Mississippi plantation owned by Calvin Candie ( Leonardo DiCaprio ). Getting inside is only half the challenge. They also need to get Broomhilda out safely. That becomes harder with Stephen ( Samuel L. Jackson ) watching their every move.
 Tarantino uses the situation to build tense conversations that sometimes erupt into violence. At the center of it all is Django’s determination to rescue his wife from slavery.
 Foxx drives Django’s noble cause, while Waltz gives Schultz an eccentric edge. Then DiCaprio enters the picture, oozing quiet menace. Even his grin makes you uneasy.
 Leonardo DiCaprio shines as Django Unchained’s villain 
 The wealth and sophistication of Candie mask little of his vile disposition. DiCaprio plays a sadistic slaver who demands subservience from all who meet him, with the actor delivering his abrupt swings between gracious and menacing with alarming effect.
 It was a departure from DiCaprio’s recent roles in romantic and action features, where winning over the audience has generally been paramount. Here there was no need to gain any sympathy or respect for the character, simply make us fearful of his intentions.
 We caught up with DiCaprio ahead of Django Unchained’s release to speak about his villainous turn and how he became involved with the project.
 Hit play on the video below to hear Leonardo DiCaprio talk about Django Unchained and how he got on board with the project.
 The role earned DiCaprio his second career Golden Globe nomination for Best Supporting Actor. Django Unchained went on to become a box office hit, raking in over $425m globally. Tarantino won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay, and Christoph Waltz won the award for Best Supporting Actor.
 Working with Tarantino again on ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood’ 
 DiCaprio was tasked with a completely different array of challenges in the pair’s next collaboration, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019). He portrayed Rick Dalton, a fading actor coming to terms with a shifting film landscape. Opposite him was Brad Pitt as his loyal stuntman Cliff Booth, allowing DiCaprio to display vulnerability, levity and exasperation at times.
 Rick crumbles slightly following his latest humbling day on a film set, whilst Candie commands total dominion over all that surrounds him. Two contrasting performances by DiCaprio that illustrate the breadth of talent the actor possesses.
 His performance netted DiCaprio a Best Actor nomination at the Oscars and continues his run of impressive work under Tarantino .
 Django Unchained is currently streaming on Pluto TV. It is also available on DVD, Blu-ray and digital platforms such as Amazon.
